git-merge-mechanics.rationale: Conflict explanation verified by execution: same line changed differently conflicts while a one-sided change further down the same file merges; directly adjacent edits conflict; one unchanged line between edits merges cleanly (ort, Git 2.53.0 and Apple Git 2.50.1). FF output with no new objects, ort message, zdiff3 base section and rerere messages re-run. merge-strategies (2.56 docs): recursive is a synonym for ort since 2.50, recursive was default until 2.33. Verifier replaced the author's lab note with a reader-facing sentence and put the 'recursive' success message in a code span (it otherwise linked to core 'recursion'). Letter-markup analogy kept.

questionsRewritten.git-merge-rebase-q1: Fast-forward prediction (still tested by git-merge-rebase-q8) replaced by a conflict-cause diagnosis because the lesson's one question should test its conflict mechanics. Verifier executed the exact scenario: timeout conflicts, return 5 merges automatically, zdiff3 shows base 30; adjacent-line note confirmed. All distractors checked; no edit.

git-rebase-replay.rationale: No maths, no question changes. Re-executed on Git 2.53.0: rebase gives replayed commits new IDs; during a rebase conflict --ours is the upstream side with already-replayed commits (45) and --theirs the commit being replayed (60), marker '>>>>>>> <id> (feat 60)'; --fixup + --autosquash folds into the target; --onto moves only the two dependent commits while plain git rebase api tries to replay old X and conflicts; merge-base --fork-point finds X. Margin-notes analogy kept (maps replay, new parent/hash, reflog; limit: shared history).

git-shared-history.rationale: Bisect estimate kept as one reference formula with a standalone In words line (about 10 tests for 1,000 commits); substitution line removed. Verifier re-executed: push rejected (fetch first); --force-with-lease rejected '(stale info)' without fetch; after fetch, --force-if-includes rejected '(remote ref updated since checkout)' while plain lease forced the update and removed the teammate commit; squash merge has one parent, branch -d refuses, a second squash conflicts; cherry-pick -x appends the source ID; bisect over 1,001 commits prints 'roughly 9 steps' and needed 10 answers. log2(1000)=9.97, log2(1e6)=19.93. No analogy needed.

git-ranges-undo.rationale: Lesson file unchanged (range and undo tables). Re-executed: pull divergence fatal plus three pull.* hints; feat..main = E, main..feat = C,D, three-dot = C,D,E; diff two-dot shows main-only changes as deletions, three-dot does not; revert of a merge without -m errors, -m 1 removes the feature, re-merge brings only the fix, reverting the revert restores it. No analogy.

git-progressive-rollouts.rationale: Expected-canary-errors relationship kept as one reference card; visible prose explains it in words and the example keeps the numbers (2,000 rps x 1 % x 600 s = 12,000 requests, ~12 errors; low-traffic case 120 requests, 0.12 errors; recomputed). Visible rollback-signal paragraph checked against the SRE Workbook (concurrent control, enough traffic, time-of-day noise); verifier replaced 'enough requests to rule out noise' with 'chance is an unlikely explanation'. Restaurant trial-dish analogy kept.

questionsRewritten.git-cd-release-q7: Expected-error arithmetic replaced by choosing the strongest rollback signal. Verifier hedged option D's explanation (the SRE Workbook notes a bad canary can also harm the control, so an equal rise makes the release unlikely rather than impossible), replaced 'rule out noise' in the key, and added to the worked example that the baseline count is equally noisy: under a Poisson assumption P(canary - baseline >= 3 | both mean 6) = 0.23, P(X >= 9 | 6) = 0.15, sqrt(6) = 2.45, and 1.5 % of the implied 3,000 requests = 45. Key unchanged.

git-schema-rollback.rationale: No maths. Expand-and-contract steps match Fowler's ParallelChange. Street-renaming analogy kept: new sign beside old = expand, both addresses = dual write, record updates = backfill, firms switching = switch reads, old signs removed last = contract; limit (many concurrent writers) is the real hazard.

git-semver-contracts.rationale: Lesson unchanged and concept-first. Verifier re-ran node-semver 7.7.4: ^0.2.3 accepts 0.2.9 only among q4's options, ^1.2.3 rejects 1.3.0-beta.1, q5 precedence order reproduced, build metadata compares equal; semver.org 2.0.0 text confirms precedence and metadata rules. No analogy needed.

git-release-automation-metrics.rationale: Redundant CFR/DRR ratio card removed; the 40-deployment example (3/40 = 7.5 %, 2/40 = 5 %) stays in prose. DORA guide re-fetched: throughput = change lead time, deployment frequency, failed deployment recovery time; instability = change fail rate, deployment rework rate, with the quoted definitions and pitfalls. describe ('v1.2.0-10-g<id>', --tags 'v1.3.0', exact tag prints 'v1.2.0') and tag sorting (default puts v2.0.0-rc.1 above v2.0.0; versionsort.suffix=- reverses it) re-executed. Conventional Commits mapping checked. No analogy.

questionsRewritten.git-cd-release-q12: Definition-recall multi replaced by an applied scenario; key [0,1,2] recomputed (4/50 = 8 % change fail rate, 2/50 = 4 % deployment rework rate, 2-day median = change lead time); distractors contradict DORA's speed-and-stability finding and its goal/competing pitfalls. No edit.

git-snapshots-objects.rationale: Short structural lesson; the object table and real cat-file output show the model more precisely than a comparison.

git-content-hashes.rationale: Shelf code computed from the text maps object ID = hash of content, dedupe of identical copies and immutability (edit = new shelf). Limit now says IDs are fixed by bytes, changes ripple up trees and old objects go only once unreferenced (git-gc docs). Kept with that correction.

git-object-formats.rationale: Status and encoding facts (hash sizes, hex length, Git 3.0 plan); no mechanism a comparison would clarify.

git-refs-index.rationale: Bookmarks (branch refs) and a clip (HEAD) on an append-only notebook map committing, cheap branching and detached HEAD; limit names the commit graph and gc of unreachable commits. Accurate per Pro Git refs chapter and the verifier's detached-HEAD run. Kept.

git-storage-recovery.rationale: Browser history maps the reflog as a local record of past ref positions that lets you return to an unreferenced commit and keeps it from pruning; limit distinguishes ref updates from uncommitted edits and expiry/gc deletion. Verifier softened 'only on your own machine' to 'usually' (browsers can sync). Kept.

git-merge-mechanics.rationale: Two marked-up copies compared with the original draft maps merge base, ours/theirs and one-sided vs two-sided changes; limit (text not meaning; adjacent lines conflict; distant edits can break each other) verified by execution. Kept.

git-rebase-replay.rationale: Copying margin notes into a new edition maps replaying commits onto a new base, new parents/hashes, rework on conflicts and originals still reachable via the reflog; limit points to shared-history divergence. Kept.

git-shared-history.rationale: Force-push checks and squash/bisect/cherry-pick are clearest as commands; the previous lesson's margin-notes analogy already covers others keeping old copies.

git-ranges-undo.rationale: Range and undo reference tables; set-style reasoning is shown directly.

git-integration-flow.rationale: The integrate-every-2-weeks vs daily ASCII diagram already provides the concrete picture.

git-gitflow-releases.rationale: Procedural branch model; the table and hotfix command template are the clearest form.

git-trunk-feature-flags.rationale: The flag code sketch and branch-by-abstraction steps are already concrete.

git-release-branch-choices.rationale: Decision guide and comparison table; an analogy would add length only.

git-review-standard.rationale: Review guidance and size rules; examples in the questions are clearer than an analogy.

git-review-feedback.rationale: Worked code review: the code itself is the concrete example.

git-review-flow-policy.rationale: Policy and tooling settings (branch protection, CODEOWNERS) are best stated directly.

git-ci-feedback.rationale: Pipeline anatomy is shown by a diagram plus a real workflow file.

git-ci-speed-flakes.rationale: The cost/time trade-off is clearer from the numeric example than from a comparison.

git-ci-flaky-tests.rationale: Ignored random smoke alarm maps flaky tests eroding trust in red builds, a point Google's 2016 post makes itself; limit says intermittent failures can be real races. Verifier corrected the limit's claim about the usual cause of false alarms. Kept.

git-ci-merged-artefacts.rationale: Shipping the sealed, inspected crate maps build once/deploy many with the digest as the seal and rebuilds as repacking; limit covers per-environment configuration and reproducible builds. Kept.

git-ci-security.rationale: Security rules are best stated directly; an analogy risks softening them.

git-delivery-deployment.rationale: Set built behind the curtain maps deploy vs release via a flag and flag-off rollback; limit (hidden code still loads/initialises/shares data; flags don't undo side effects) matches the lesson's caveats and Fowler's feature toggles. Kept.

git-progressive-rollouts.rationale: Trialling a dish on a few tables against same-evening diners maps canary vs concurrent baseline and early stop; limit covers small-sample noise and shared systems, consistent with the SRE Workbook. Kept.

git-schema-rollback.rationale: Renaming a street in stages maps expand, dual write, backfill, switch reads and contract; limit names concurrent writers, the real hazard in Fowler's ParallelChange. Kept.

git-semver-contracts.rationale: Rule lesson; version examples and range tables are the clearest teaching device.

git-release-automation-metrics.rationale: Tooling commands and metric definitions; the worked examples suffice.
